8 09-09-2024

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, the State and the opposite party no.2.
2.

The petitioner, who is husband of opposite party no.2, apprehends arrest in a case registered for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 307, 406, 323, 341, 504/34 the IPC and  of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
3. Allegation against the petitioner is of matrimonial cruelty and demand of dowry.
4. While denying the allegations, learned counsel for the petitioner has filed supplementary affidavit.

In paragraph 2 of the supplementary affidavit, it is submitted that by order dated 27.9.2023, passed in Matrimonial Case No.128 of 2022, by the Principal Judge, Family Court,
Begusarai petitioner was directed to pay maintenance amount of Rs.8,000/- per month to opposite party no.2 since the date of filing of the case, i.e., Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.72749 of 2023(8)
dt.09-09-2024 20.8.2022.

entities.text:
Principal Judge, Family Court,
Begusarai petitioner
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that in the maintenance case, petitioner has deposited Rs.50,000/- in the Court Nazarat, Begusarai.

He has further stated that the order dated Manoj Kumar Sharma vs The State Of Bihar on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135441848/
1 27.9.2023 is ex-party and the petitioner has challenged the same before this Court.
5. Learned counsel for the State and opposite party no.2 oppose the prayer for bail.
6. In the facts and circumstances of the case, in the event of arrest/surrender within a period of eight weeks from today, above-named petitioner be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.
10,000/- (ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Begusarai in Complaint Case No. 510C/2022, subject to the conditions laid down under section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure with the condition that the petitioner shall regularly pay the maintenance to opposite party no.2 as per order passed by the Family Court in the maintenance case.
Shashi (Prabhat Kumar Singh, J)
